title: Risk factors for not finishing an ultramarathon: 4-year study in 23,996 race starters, SAFER XXI
authors: Sewry N, Schwellnus MP, Borjesson M, Swanevelder S, Jordaan E
journal: The Journal of Sports Medicine and Physical Fitness
population: Starters of the 56-km Two Oceans ultramarathon who completed a pre-race medical screening questionnaire
findings: The abstract describes a prospective, cross-sectional study. DNF risk was higher with older age and in females (P < 0.0001).

After adjusting for age and sex, significant univariate risk factors were fewer years of running (P < 0.0001), less previous race experience (P < 0.0001), less training/racing per week (P = 0.0002), lower average weekly training distance (P = 0.0016) and slower race vs training speed (P < 0.0001).
Higher average wet-bulb globe temperature on race day increased DNF risk (P < 0.0001).
Lack of allergies was also associated with DNF (P = 0.0100).
limitations: One 56-km race; univariate (age/sex-adjusted) associations from self-reported questionnaires; no effect sizes or thresholds in the abstract; may not transfer to 100-mile races.
implications: Implement a pre-race readiness check using three training-derived DNF flags: low weekly training distance, low sessions per week, and race goal pace that is fast relative to recent training pace. Show as messages, not a hard block.
Add heat adjustment: raise the finish-risk flag and slow the planned pace when forecast WBGT is high.
No numeric thresholds are justified by the abstract; calibrate against the athlete's own history.

verification.notes: Crossref (2022-04, first author Sewry) and Europe PMC abstract re-fetched with P-values. Design changed from prospective-cohort to cross-sectional to match the abstract's own label; B kept because of n = 23,996. Researcher wording 'slower race vs training speed' implies a slow goal pace; the abstract does not say which direction of mismatch, so the implication was reworded to a mismatch flag.
